hints: Focus on what bond actually breaks in free-radical substitution, C-H or C-C?
The first propagation step from ethane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3$, can only give the ethyl radical $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\bullet$, not a methyl radical.
Remember chlorination does not stop at one substitution, so think about what radicals form when $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ and further chlorinated products react with $\text{Cl}\bullet$.
walkthrough:
**Recall the normal propagation steps**

Free-radical substitution replaces C-H with C-Cl. It does not break the C-C skeleton.

Initiation:
$$\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{Cl}\bullet$$

First propagation:
$$\text{Cl}\bullet + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\bullet + \text{HCl}$$

**Check radical 1**

$\text{CH}_3\bullet$ would need the C-C bond in ethane to split.

That is cracking or homolysis of the carbon chain, not hydrogen abstraction by $\text{Cl}\bullet$. So 1 is not generated.

**Allow for further substitution**

The product $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ can react again with $\text{Cl}\bullet$:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{ClCH}_2\bullet + \text{HCl}$$
So radical 2 is formed.

**Continue to di- and tri-chloro products**

Once you have $\text{CH}_3\text{CHCl}_2$, hydrogen abstraction gives:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHCl}_2 + \text{Cl}\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CCl}_2\bullet + \text{HCl}$$
So radical 3 is also formed in later propagation cycles. Therefore 2 and 3 only are correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This states 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Radicals 2 and 3 are possible from further chlorination, but 1, $\text{CH}_3\bullet$, requires C-C bond cleavage which does not occur in free-radical substitution.
options.B: Incorrect. This states 1 and 2 only are correct. It correctly includes 2 but wrongly includes 1 and wrongly excludes 3. $\text{CH}_3\bullet$ is not formed, while $\text{CH}_3\text{CCl}_2\bullet$ is formed from a polychlorinated intermediate.
options.C: Correct. This states 2 and 3 only are correct. Both $\text{CH}_2\text{ClCH}_2\bullet$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CCl}_2\bullet$ arise by $\text{Cl}\bullet$ abstracting H from $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ and from more highly chlorinated products. $\text{CH}_3\bullet$ is not formed.
options.D: Incorrect. This states 1 only is correct. $\text{CH}_3\bullet$ is the one radical that cannot be generated here, because substitution attacks C-H bonds and leaves the C-C bond of ethane intact.
